title: Rabbi Tanchum bar Yudan (or Yehudah)
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: Model-assisted translation, editorially reviewed; publication authorized by Joshua Waxman.

paragraphs: He is mentioned in Jerusalem Talmud Berakhot 6:1, folio 39b, saying on Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba’s words that one must say “Blessed be the name of His glorious kingdom forever and ever.” (Hyman explains this as what Yuchasin meant in citing Rabbi Tanchum bar Yudan with Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba, and Seder HaDorot wrote, “I have not found it.”) There, at the end of chapter 7 and in 9:5, he said that one must bless both for the attribute of mercy and for the attribute of judgment (there it reads Rabbi Tanchuma ben Yehudah, but at the beginning of Vayikra Rabbah, chapter 24, the statement is cited as Rabbi Tanchum bar Yudan). Jerusalem Talmud Yoma 1:1, folio 2b; 2:1, folio 8b.

notes.text: כאנת is understood as כונת. The explanation of Yuchasin’s intention remains Hyman’s. The Yoma chapter/halakhah/folio locations are Jerusalem Talmud; their historical pagination is not silently equated with Bavli pages.

The consulted Jerusalem Talmud Berakhot 6:1 directly names Tanchum bar Yudan in the Barukh Shem instruction. The historical folio references and Hyman’s explanation of Yuchasin’s intention remain distinct from independently establishing the cited editions.
